name: Distributed systems fundamentals
description: Reason about partial failure, network partitions, replication, consistency, coordination, time and failure domains.

name: Event-driven architecture
description: Design asynchronous systems with explicit event contracts, ownership, ordering, replay, schema evolution and failure handling.

name: Idempotency
description: Make retried requests and redelivered messages safe using idempotency keys, deduplication boundaries and durable state.

name: Delivery semantics
description: Understand at-most-once, at-least-once and effectively-once processing and design consumers for duplicates and failures.

name: Timeouts, retries and jitter
description: Use bounded timeouts and retry appropriate failures with exponential backoff and jitter without amplifying outages.

name: Circuit breakers
description: Protect services from unhealthy dependencies and understand interaction with retries, timeouts and fallbacks.

name: Rate limiting and backpressure
description: Control demand with rate limits, bounded queues, flow control and load shedding.

name: Caching strategies
description: Understand cache-aside, invalidation, TTLs, consistency, hot keys, stampedes and cache failure modes.

name: API design and evolution
description: Design stable APIs with clear contracts, errors, pagination, idempotency, compatibility and deprecation strategies.

name: Database transactions and isolation
description: Understand ACID, MVCC, isolation levels, anomalies, locks, deadlocks and transaction boundaries.

name: Database indexing and query optimization
description: Use execution plans, statistics, indexes and workload evidence to diagnose database performance.

name: Data modeling and access patterns
description: Model data from access patterns, invariants, cardinality, lifecycle and scale.

name: Horizontal partitioning and sharding
description: Understand shard-key selection, hotspots, resharding, fan-out queries and routing.

name: Replication and consistency models
description: Reason about replication lag, read consistency, quorum concepts and strong versus eventual consistency.

name: Concurrency control
description: Understand optimistic and pessimistic concurrency, atomic operations, races and lost updates.

name: Observability
description: Design useful logs, metrics and traces and connect telemetry to user-visible outcomes.

name: SLIs, SLOs and error budgets
description: Define reliability from the user's perspective and use error budgets and burn-rate signals to balance reliability and delivery.

name: Incident response and blameless postmortems
description: Mitigate incidents systematically, communicate clearly and turn contributing factors into durable improvements.

name: Graceful degradation
description: Preserve critical functionality during overload or dependency failure using fallbacks and load shedding.

name: Capacity planning
description: Estimate throughput, concurrency, storage and saturation points and validate assumptions against production behavior.

name: Load and performance testing
description: Model representative workloads and interpret latency percentiles, throughput, errors and saturation.

name: Secure-by-design development
description: Treat authentication, authorization, secrets, validation, encryption and dependency risk as design concerns.

name: Threat modeling
description: Identify assets, trust boundaries, threats and mitigations during system design.

name: Architecture Decision Records
description: Record consequential architectural decisions, context, alternatives and trade-offs.

name: Modular monolith
description: Prefer strong internal boundaries without distributed-systems overhead when independent deployment is not justified.

name: Microservices
description: Understand service boundaries, independent deployment, data ownership and operational costs; use them when constraints justify them.

name: API gateway pattern
description: Understand routing, authentication, policy enforcement, rate limiting and aggregation at service boundaries.

name: Service discovery
description: Understand dynamic endpoint discovery, health and DNS or registry-based service location.

name: DORA metrics
description: Use delivery and stability measures as system-level feedback rather than simplistic individual productivity scores.

name: Trunk-based development
description: Keep integration continuous through small changes, short-lived branches, automated tests and feature controls.

name: Feature flags
description: Decouple deployment from release, support progressive rollout and remove stale flags.

name: AI-assisted software engineering
description: Use coding agents for investigation and implementation while retaining human ownership of architecture, verification and production outcomes.

name: Repository instructions for coding agents
description: Maintain concise repository instructions such as AGENTS.md covering architecture, testing, conventions and constraints.

name: Zero trust architecture
description: Understand identity-centric security, least privilege and continuous verification across service boundaries.

name: Transactional Outbox
description: Practice solving the database-and-message dual-write problem with a durable outbox and idempotent consumers.

name: Saga pattern
description: Coordinate multi-service transactions with local transactions and compensations; compare orchestration and choreography.

name: Change Data Capture
description: Understand log-based data-change propagation and when CDC is preferable to application publishing or polling.

name: Event schema evolution
description: Evolve asynchronous contracts safely using compatibility rules, tolerant consumers and controlled migrations.

name: Workflow orchestration
description: Model long-running failure-prone business processes durably and compare workflow engines with queues and state machines.

name: Domain-driven design
description: Use bounded contexts and ubiquitous language to manage complex domains without turning patterns into ceremony.

name: Evolutionary architecture
description: Design architectures that can change incrementally and protect important characteristics with feedback.

name: Strangler Fig migration
description: Modernize systems incrementally by routing functionality from legacy components to new implementations.

name: Progressive delivery
description: Use canary and phased rollouts with observability and rollback criteria to reduce change risk.

name: Cost-aware architecture / FinOps
description: Include compute, storage, network and managed-service economics in architecture decisions.

name: Context engineering
description: Curate instructions, retrieved knowledge, tools and context boundaries for effective AI-assisted engineering.

name: Agent Skills
description: Experiment with modular reusable agent capabilities and distinguish them from repository instructions and prompts.

name: Agent evaluation and verification
description: Evaluate nondeterministic agent behavior with repeatable tasks, tests, traces and human review.

name: CQRS
description: Understand separating command and query models and the consistency and operational complexity it introduces.

name: Event sourcing
description: Understand event logs as source of truth, projections, replay and snapshots without treating the pattern as a default.

name: Consensus and Raft
description: Understand quorum, leader election, terms, replicated logs and network partitions.

name: Logical clocks and causal ordering
description: Understand Lamport and vector-clock concepts and why wall-clock timestamps cannot establish causality.

name: CRDTs
description: Understand convergent replicated data structures and coordination-free conflict resolution.

name: Distributed locking
description: Understand leases, fencing tokens and why naive distributed locks can violate correctness.

name: Chaos engineering
description: Use controlled failure injection to validate resilience hypotheses after foundational reliability practices are established.

name: Platform engineering
description: Understand internal developer platforms, paved roads and self-service capabilities.

name: RAG architecture
description: Understand retrieval, chunking, embeddings, ranking, permissions, grounding and evaluation.

name: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
description: Understand MCP interoperability and trust boundaries while recognizing when direct APIs or CLIs are simpler.

name: Service mesh by default
description: Do not introduce a service mesh without concrete traffic policy, identity or observability needs that justify its operational cost.

name: Premature microservice decomposition
description: Avoid independently deployed services before boundaries, scaling needs or ownership justify distributed-systems complexity.

name: Exactly-once assumptions
description: Avoid designing correctness around simplistic exactly-once claims; model retries, duplicates and side effects explicitly.

name: Unbounded retries and queues
description: Avoid retry loops and queues without explicit limits, backpressure, expiry and failure handling.

name: Coding throughput as productivity
description: Do not equate lines of code, commits or AI-generated volume with engineering productivity.

name: Linux
description: Understand processes, signals, filesystems, permissions, networking, resource limits and common production diagnostics.

name: Containers
description: Understand images, layers, namespaces, cgroups, networking, registries and container lifecycle.

name: Kubernetes
description: Be production-confident with workloads, probes, requests and limits, autoscaling, networking, rollouts and failure diagnosis.

name: Google Cloud Platform
description: Understand IAM, networking, compute, managed data services, messaging, observability, quotas and cost.

name: PostgreSQL
description: Know planner and statistics, indexing, MVCC, VACUUM, WAL, locks, replication, partitioning and connection management.

name: Redis
description: Understand caching, data structures, persistence, eviction, replication, clustering, hot keys and failure modes.

name: GCP Pub/Sub
description: Understand delivery semantics, ordering, retries, dead-letter topics, flow control, scaling, quotas and monitoring.

name: Object storage
description: Understand S3/GCS-style storage semantics, lifecycle, multipart transfer, signed access and architecture use cases.

name: Managed relational databases
description: Understand backups, PITR, replicas, failover, maintenance, connection limits and managed-service trade-offs.

name: Apache Kafka
description: Gain hands-on experience with partitions, consumer groups, offsets, ordering, retention, rebalancing and operations.

name: BigQuery
description: Understand analytical modeling, partitioning, clustering, query cost and OLAP versus OLTP boundaries.

name: ClickHouse
description: Gain experience with columnar OLAP workloads and compare it with PostgreSQL and warehouse systems.

name: Cassandra / Dynamo-style databases
description: Understand partition keys, consistent hashing, quorum behavior, LSM storage, compaction and eventual consistency.

name: Temporal
description: Explore durable workflow execution and compare it with queues, sagas and hand-built state machines.

name: Content delivery networks
description: Understand edge caching, cache keys, invalidation, origin protection and latency/cost trade-offs.

name: Elasticsearch / OpenSearch
description: Understand inverted indexes, mappings, shards, replicas and search workloads without using it as a default transactional store.

name: Apache Iceberg
description: Understand analytical table formats, snapshots, schema evolution and lakehouse architecture.

name: Vector databases
description: Understand vector indexing, similarity retrieval, metadata filtering and semantic-search/RAG trade-offs.

name: Service mesh
description: Understand mTLS, traffic policy and telemetry benefits versus infrastructure and debugging complexity.

name: AWS
description: Maintain cloud-portable literacy across compute, IAM, networking, storage, messaging and databases.

name: Cloudflare
description: Understand edge compute, CDN, DNS, security and globally distributed application capabilities.

name: Serverless platforms
description: Understand event-driven execution, scaling, cold starts, limits and cost models.

name: Git
description: Use branching, rebasing, bisect, reflog and history investigation confidently and understand Git's object model.

name: Docker
description: Build secure, minimal and reproducible images and diagnose container build and runtime problems.

name: OpenTelemetry
description: Instrument vendor-neutral telemetry and understand context propagation, sampling, semantic conventions and collectors.

name: Prometheus
description: Understand metric types, labels and cardinality, PromQL, recording rules and alerting.

name: Grafana
description: Create diagnostic dashboards around service health, SLOs and business-relevant signals.

name: Go pprof
description: Diagnose CPU, heap, allocation, goroutine, mutex and blocking problems in Go services.

name: EXPLAIN / EXPLAIN ANALYZE
description: Read PostgreSQL plans and connect estimates, scans, joins, buffers and statistics to query performance.

name: Terraform / OpenTofu
description: Understand infrastructure modules, state, plans, drift, lifecycle and safe deployment workflows.

name: GitHub Actions
description: Design CI/CD workflows with caching, artifacts, environments, security boundaries and deployment gates.

name: Static analysis and linters
description: Use automated analysis to catch correctness, security and maintainability issues early.

name: Dependency and vulnerability scanning
description: Identify vulnerable dependencies, leaked secrets and risky artifacts and maintain a remediation process.

name: Database migration tools
description: Use versioned schema migrations safely and understand expand-contract changes, compatibility, locking and rollback limitations.

name: Coding agents
description: Use coding agents for repository investigation, implementation and verification without outsourcing engineering judgment.

name: Make / task runners
description: Provide predictable build, test, lint, generation and local workflows.

name: Go execution tracer
description: Investigate scheduler, goroutine, GC and latency behavior when profiles are insufficient.

name: Helm
description: Maintain Kubernetes application packaging while recognizing templating complexity and alternatives.

name: k6
description: Create repeatable load tests and interpret latency, throughput, errors and saturation.

name: Delve
description: Debug Go processes and tests using breakpoints, goroutine inspection and runtime state.

name: Local Kubernetes environments
description: Use local clusters such as kind or minikube to reproduce Kubernetes behavior.

name: Dev Containers
description: Create reproducible development environments for onboarding, CI parity and sandboxed agent execution.

name: eBPF observability tools
description: Understand low-overhead kernel and network observability and when eBPF helps production diagnosis.

name: Go
description: Go beyond syntax into scheduler behavior, goroutines, channels, memory, GC, escape analysis, networking, profiling and API design.

name: SQL
description: Treat SQL as a core engineering language including joins, windows, CTEs, aggregation, locking and plan implications.

name: HTTP
description: Understand methods, status codes, headers, caching, conditional requests and HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 trade-offs.

name: gRPC
description: Design RPC services with deadlines, cancellation, streaming, interceptors, status semantics and observability.

name: Protocol Buffers
description: Evolve typed schemas safely using field-number discipline and compatibility rules.

name: OpenAPI
description: Use machine-readable HTTP API contracts for documentation, validation, compatibility and generation.

name: Regular expressions
description: Use regex safely while understanding readability, performance and ReDoS risks.

name: Bash / shell scripting
description: Automate tasks safely with quoting, pipes, exit handling and portable command composition.

name: JSON Schema
description: Use machine-readable validation for JSON payloads and configuration and understand schema evolution.

name: Python
description: Maintain enough Python literacy for automation, data and AI tooling and cross-team collaboration.

name: WebAssembly
description: Understand sandboxed portable execution and emerging server-side and plugin use cases.

name: TCP and connection lifecycle
description: Understand TCP connection establishment, retransmission, flow and congestion control, keepalives, resets and how connection behavior affects backend latency and reliability.

name: DNS
description: Understand recursive resolution, authoritative servers, caching, TTLs, service discovery and DNS-related production failure modes.

name: TLS and PKI
description: Understand TLS handshakes, certificates, trust chains, certificate rotation, SNI and the security and latency implications of encrypted transport.

name: Load balancing
description: Understand L4 and L7 balancing, health checks, algorithms, connection draining, sticky sessions and failure behavior.

name: Connection pooling
description: Size and operate database and HTTP connection pools using concurrency, latency and downstream capacity rather than arbitrary defaults.

name: Database storage internals
description: Understand pages, B-trees, LSM trees, WAL, checkpoints, compaction and how storage-engine design shapes database behavior.

name: MVCC and vacuuming
description: Understand row versions, snapshots, dead tuples, vacuuming and how long transactions and write-heavy workloads affect MVCC databases.

name: Database replication and failover
description: Understand physical and logical replication, lag, failover, split-brain risks, read replicas and recovery objectives.

name: OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect
description: Understand authorization flows, tokens, scopes, clients, resource servers and the role of OIDC for authentication.

name: Authorization models
description: Understand RBAC, ABAC, relationship-based authorization, policy enforcement and how authorization boundaries evolve with systems.

name: Secrets management
description: Manage credentials and keys with centralized secret stores, rotation, short-lived identity and least-privilege access.

name: Software supply-chain security
description: Understand dependency provenance, SBOMs, artifact signing, build integrity and controls that reduce software supply-chain risk.

name: API security and abuse prevention
description: Design APIs against broken authorization, injection, SSRF, replay, credential abuse and resource-exhaustion attacks.

name: Memory management and garbage collection
description: Reason about allocation, heap growth, GC pauses, memory leaks and runtime behavior when diagnosing backend performance.

name: OS scheduling and resource isolation
description: Understand CPU scheduling, cgroups, quotas, throttling and noisy-neighbor effects across containers and services.

name: Queues and load shedding
description: Use bounded queues, admission control and load shedding to keep overloaded systems stable rather than accumulating unbounded work.

name: Distributed tracing context propagation
description: Understand trace and baggage propagation across synchronous and asynchronous boundaries and avoid broken or excessively expensive traces.

name: Data retention and lifecycle
description: Design retention, archival, deletion and backup policies around product needs, cost, privacy and recovery requirements.

name: Backup and disaster recovery
description: Define RPO and RTO, validate backups through restoration, and design recovery procedures for realistic failure scenarios.

name: Multi-region architecture
description: Understand active-passive and active-active designs, latency, data placement, consistency, failover and operational complexity across regions.

name: Cloud IAM
description: Design workload and human identities with least privilege, short-lived credentials, role boundaries and auditable access.

name: Policy as code
description: Express infrastructure, security and deployment policies as reviewable and testable code with automated enforcement.

name: Stream processing
description: Understand event time, processing time, windows, watermarks, state, checkpoints and late data in continuous data processing.

name: Data contracts
description: Define ownership, schemas, semantics, compatibility and quality expectations for data exchanged between producers and consumers.

name: AI tool calling and structured outputs
description: Design reliable model-to-system interactions using explicit tool contracts, structured outputs, validation and bounded permissions.

name: Agent observability
description: Trace agent decisions, tool calls, latency, cost and failures so nondeterministic workflows can be evaluated and operated.

name: Agent security and sandboxing
description: Treat prompts, retrieved content and tools as trust boundaries and constrain agent execution with permissions, isolation and validation.

name: Durable agent workflows
description: Explore checkpointing, resumability, human approval and durable execution for long-running agentic processes.

name: Model routing and AI gateways
description: Understand centralized model access, routing, policy, observability, caching, fallback and cost controls across AI providers.

name: Post-quantum cryptography readiness
description: Understand cryptographic agility, migration planning and why long-lived sensitive systems should track post-quantum standards.

name: WebSockets and Server-Sent Events
description: Understand long-lived server-client communication, connection management, backpressure, reconnection and when SSE or WebSockets fit.

name: CloudEvents
description: Use a common event-envelope specification to improve interoperability and metadata consistency across event-driven systems.
